name: P719 internal AMM mints its swap output and burns its swap input
summary: P719 is its own market maker: BNB sent to the token buys and tokens sent to it sell, both priced constant-product from its BNB and token balances. Buys minted 1.55x the quoted output instead of debiting the token reserve and sells burned their input, so the reserves' product fell with every swap; buying through many helpers and then selling drained the BNB reserve.
notes: Runtime is unverified; the pricing and the mint/burn asymmetry were reconstructed from the trace's Transfer events and the token's balances. Reset: the deployer's launch transaction 0xcff82c29 (block 42965578, 154 blocks after deployment, through 0x8c5ea018) funded the token's BNB reserve with 623.48 BNB, set the flag in the lowest byte of packed slot 0x6, zero from deployment and never cleared, and recorded the trading-start block in slot 0xa. A replay of the anchor with that flag cleared reverts, so this first opening of trading resets the age (rule 8).

Loss is the token contract's net BNB outflow per transaction: the anchor (fees to the token's own wallets included, as they left the reserve backing holders) and the copycat 0xac8107fc by 0xcd5e7b69, which repeated the buy/sell loop through the same selector two days later. Other later outflows are plain sells without buys in the same tx.
